metadata.title: Curative Title Explained by a Florida Probate Attorney
metadata.author: Logan Fullmer
metadata.shortDescription:
Curative title deals sound simple until you find out the heir who says she's the only sibling actually has 13 brothers and sisters. Al Nicoletti is a high-volume Florida probate attorney who has handled more than 2,000 probates, plus the quiet titles, partitions, and title problems that come with messy real estate deals.

In this episode of Dirty Deeds, Al and Logan Fullmer walk through how probate really works in curative title deals: why one property often needs two or three probates, the documents to gather before you ever call an attorney, the difference between summary and formal administration in Florida, and what happens when all you have is a copy of the will.

They also cover how creditors work in probate, when a partition lawsuit makes sense, how a quiet title can clear what a probate can't, and why you should get the title underwriter's sign-off before you file anything.

You'll learn:
- How to figure out who the real heirs are, and why people leave some out
- Why many curative title deals need more than one probate
- What documents to collect before you call a probate attorney
- The mistake most probate attorneys make on investor deals
- Summary vs. formal administration in Florida
- What happens when there's only a copy of the will
- When to use a partition lawsuit, and what it costs
- How quiet title actions clear title when probate isn't enough
